newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen flat-off $0.50- trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen flat-off $0.50- trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by light packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were expected to range from $58.00 to $59.50. Some packer buyers said they bought enough hogs to cover Wednesday needs.
Illinois buyers said top hog prices at plants could range from $57.50 to $58.00.
Indiana/Ohio buyers said they expect top hog prices at the plant to range from $56.00 to $57.00.
IBP Inc, Excel Corp, Swift and Co and John Morrell and Co officials said their respective companies were trimming hog slaughter operations due to unprofitable operating margins.

Depending on company and plant needs, operations were being trimmed either one hour per shift or to a 32-hour work week from a normal 40- to 48-hour week, officials said. They declined to comment on how long the cutbacks would remain in effect.
Reduced kills were reflected in Monday's hog slaughter estimate. Slaughter was pegged by USDA at 330,000 head, compared with 366,000 a week ago and 331,000 a year ago.
